extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: A training environment for software engineering agents, combining real-world Python tasks with pre-configured executable environments and expert-validated test cases.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: SWE-Gym contains 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: SWE-Gym Raw, a large set of Python GitHub issues without executable environments (64,689 instances spanning 358 Python repositories).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Creating executable environments with pre-installed dependencies for each task instance using relevant configuration files, CI scripts, or documentation from the repository snapshot.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Expert-validated test cases, constructed in close alignment with SWE-Bench.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Pre-built Docker images for each instance, totaling 6 TB, are publicly released.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer’s productivity and accessibility across industries.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Task success probability follows a long-tail distribution, where more samples increase solved instances, but introduces a bias toward easier tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include potential dataset bias and the need for more advanced policy optimization methods.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training software engineering agents, verifier models, and scaling agent performance with inference-time and training-time data scaling.
